description_en: Facing south, the Suntvāḥ Phalcā (North) stands east of the street that joins Suntvāḥ (Sun Ṭola) with the Sālkhā Ṭola. Among the three rest houses at Suntvāḥ (twophalcās and asataḥ), Suntvāḥ Phalcā (North) is the one north of Suntvāḥ Phalcā (South) (SKH0224). The other rest house of the area, Suntvāḥ Sataḥ (SKH0221), is situated southwest of this Phalcā across the Street. Likewise, Lāṃkva Hiti is constructed to the southeast of this Phalcā. The Phalcā’s traditional architecture is already lost and is now a plain concrete structure of two bays and two floors. The ground floor is open from two sides (south and west) while one half of the upper floor is closed for a room with the other half left open as a terrace. The upper floor is being used by a Śreṣṭha family living in the adjoining house north of the Phalcā.The details of the initial construction of the Phalcā are unclear. The local oral tradition credits Candra Nārāyaṇa Śreṣṭha, an ancestor of the Śreṣṭha family living in the adjoining building, for commissioning the construction of this Phalcā during the partyless Pañcāyata rule (1961 CE-1990 CE). However, there is no historic source to support the statement. It used to be a three-bay Phalcā with artistic pillars. After it collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes, Uttama Nārāyaṇa Śreṣṭha, the grandson of Candra Nārāyaṇa, funded the reconstruction of the Phalcā in 2016 CE (local resident, Śreṣṭha, male, age 54). The traditional architecture of the Phalcā was not adopted in the reconstruction.Four majorṭolas of Sankhu take a turn once a year to organize the annual Vajrayoginī Jātrā, which is observed for eight days starting from the full moon day of Caitra. When Suntvāḥ organizes the Jātrā once in every four years, the statues of the deities are brought into the town from the Mhāsukhvāḥmāju Dyaḥchẽ (SKH0550) and placed at the Suntvāḥ Sataḥ. In the course of the Jātrā, locals performbhajanas at this Phalcā every evening. No other socio-cultural activities take place here.There are three rest houses at Suntvāḥ: twophalcās and onesataḥ. Suntvāḥ Phalcā (South) is the one facing west. It stands west of Lāṃkva Hiti and south of Suntvāḥ Phalcā (North) (SKH0222). Another rest house, Suntvāḥ Sataḥ (SKH0221) is situated in front of the Phalcā to the west across the street.The monument does not appear to be aphalcāat present. It is a concrete structure of one floor with corrugated sheets laid on the roof. The two rooms with metal shutters have been rented out as shops. A grocery store operates from one room while the other room is a vegetable/fruit shop. The Suntvāḥ Ṭola Sudhara Samiti, a local committee formed for the conservation of the area, collects the rent from the shops. According to local residents, the space of the Phalcā was rented out after its reconstruction following the 2015 earthquakes.Nothing is known about the initial construction of this Phalcā. Due to the poor condition of the Phalcā, the locals reconstructed it in 2003 CE (local resident, Śreṣṭha, female, age 70). The 2015 earthquakes damaged the roof of the Phalcā and the Samiti renovated the roof and laid corrugated tin sheets.Every year on the 14thof the dark fortnight of Bhādra, Vasundharā Jātrā is observed in Sankhu. On the same day, the almsgiving festival ofpañcadānais also celebrated by making various offerings to Śākyas and Vajrācāryas. Such an offering is made here at the Phalcā as well. Likewise, aguthiof the Śreṣṭha community of Sankhu offers unhusked rice to Vasundhara when the deity’s palanquin arrives here. The event is locally known asvādānabīgu(lit. to offer unhusked rice as a charity).
description_ne: मणिशैल महावदान अनुसार कलिगत संवत् १८०१ मा जोगदेव वज्राचार्यले वज्रयोगिनीदेवीको आज्ञाअनुसार सातवटा गाउँलाई मिलाएर शङ्ख आकारमा साँखुको निर्माण गर्दा केन्द्रमा दरवार बनाई आठवटा टोल, अष्टमातृका, नौवटा बाहाः, चार दिशामा चारवटा ढोका बनाएका थिए (V. Vajrācārya1119, p. 29-33) । ती आठवटा टोलमध्ये सुन्त्वाः (सुन टोल) पनि पर्दछ । साँखुको अन्य टोलहरू झैं यो टोलमा पनि विभिन्न ऐतिहासिक मठमन्दिर, पाटी पौवा र ढुङ्गेधाराहरू निर्मित छन् । सुन्त्वाः फल्चा (दक्षिण) सुन्त्वाःमा रहेका फल्चाहरू मध्ये एक हो । यो फल्चा सुन्त्वाःदेखि साल्खा टोल जोडिने बाटोको पूर्वपट्टी पश्चिमाभिमुख भई निर्माण गरिएको छ । यो फल्चाको पूर्वपट्टी लांक्व हिति (ढुङ्गेधारा), उत्तरमा सुन्त्वाः फल्चा (उत्तर) (SKH0222) छ भने पश्चिममा (बाटो पारी) सुन्त्वाः सतः (SKH0221) देख्न सकिन्छ ।हाल यो संरचना फल्चाको स्वरूमा छैन । सिमेन्ट र इँटाको प्रयोग गरी बनेको यो फल्चामा दुईवटा कोठा निकाली आधुनिक सटर हालिएको छ भने जस्तापाताको छानो राखिएको छ । एउटा कोठामा किराना पसल राखिएको छ भने अर्कोमा फलफुल तथा तरकारी पसल राखिएको छ । सुन्त्वाः टोल सुधार समितिले पसलको बाहाल उठाउदै आएको छ । फल्चाको पुनःनिर्माण पछि यसलाई बहालमा दिन थालेको स्थानीयहरुको भनाई छ ।यो फल्चाको निर्माण बारे कुनै अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । फल्चा निकै पुरानो भइसकेको र भत्कने अवस्थामा पुगेको हुनाले स्थानीयको सक्रियतामा सन् २००३ (विसं २०६०) सालमा यसको पुनःनिर्माण गरिएको थियो (local resident, Śreṣṭha, female, age 70) । सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पले फल्चाको छानो जीर्ण बनाएको थियो । सुन्त्वाः टोल सुधार समितिले केही समय पछि जस्ताको छानो हाली जीर्णोद्धार गरेको थियो ।हरेक वर्ष भाद्र कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन साँखुमा वसुन्धरादेवीको जात्रा मनाउने चलन छ । त्यो दिन साँखुमा विभिन्न ठाऊँहरूमा शाक्य वज्राचार्यहरूलाई पञ्चदान दिने पनि चलन रहेको छ । विभिन्न स्थानहरू मध्ये यो फल्चा छेउमा बसेर पनि पञ्चदान दिने परम्परा चल्दै आइरहेको छ । यसका साथै सोही दिन श्रेष्ठ समुदायको गुठीले यही ठाऊँबाट वसुन्धरादेवीलाई धान चढाउने गर्दछन् । उक्त चलनलाई 'वा दान बीगु' भन्ने गरिन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: As the Phalcā was on the verge of collapse, it was dismantled and rebuilt at the initiation of local residents. Using brick and cement, it was rebuilt as a two-bay concrete shed, making the Phalcā lose its traditional look.

After the Phalcā was reconstructed as a modern into a concrete shed of two rooms, they were rented out to local residents. The Suntvāḥ Ṭola Sudhara Samiti, a local committee for the conservation of the area, collects the rent from the shops.
The 2015 earthquakes damaged the roof of the Phalcā, which was renovated by The Suntvāḥ Ṭola Sudhara Samiti, a local committee for the conservation of the area.
